Perioperative Outcomes of Robotic-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy

Test Paper B · right pane · narrower text column, 4 sections

Background

Robotic-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) has become the dominant surgical approach for localized prostate cancer in many health systems. Whether its higher fixed cost is offset by improved perioperative outcomes remains debated.

中文对照段落：机器人辅助根治性前列腺切除术在多数医疗体系中已成为局限性前列腺癌的主要术式，但其较高的设备成本能否被围手术期结局的改善所抵消，仍存在争议。

Methods

We searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from January 2018 to June 2025. Studies comparing RARP with laparoscopic or open prostatectomy were eligible. Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

Pooled estimates were calculated with a random-effects model. Heterogeneity was quantified using the I² statistic.

Results

Twenty-seven studies comprising 8,431 patients were included. RARP was associated with lower estimated blood loss and shorter length of stay, while operative time was longer.

Positive surgical margin rates did not differ significantly between approaches.

Conclusion

RARP appears safe in the perioperative setting. Long-term oncological superiority, however, has not been demonstrated.
